destinations.heroSubtitleAbha: One visit is never enough with all the activities and experiences on offer.
destinations.introBody: On the Sarawat peaks in southwest Saudi Arabia, Abha rests like a jewel crowned in mist and beauty, wrapped in cloud summer and winter.
destinations.introP1: On the Sarawat peaks in southwest Saudi Arabia, Abha rests like a jewel crowned in mist and beauty, wrapped in cloud summer and winter. It is the bright gateway to Aseer and rich with diversity in every direction. Its cool, rainy summers have made it a leading sustainable destination, backed by deep cultural, artistic and heritage assets.
destinations.introP2: Historic fortresses tell centuries of stories—from Shamsan and Dhara to the great and small Daql forts. Heritage museums in restored homes, such as Fatima Museum and Al-Raqidi Museum, introduce visitors to Aseer's treasures.
destinations.introP3: Along Abha Valley runs one of its most famous folk markets, Tuesday Market, beside the artistic Al-Muftaha village—home to arts and the legacy of Talal Maddah.
destinations.introP4: Green fields across Abha supply flowers, grains, fruit and vegetables; locals work in trade, industry and agriculture.
destinations.introP5: Ancient yet calm as a summer dream, Abha competes globally in modern services, dining, cafés, entertainment, sport and year-round festivals and forums.
destinations.introP6: Abha—a treasure whose richness never ends and whose wonder never fades.

attractionsPage.introBody: Aseer's historic and cultural landmarks blend authenticity with natural beauty.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP1: Al Abu Sirah palaces rise above the tranquil village of Al-Azizah among the villages of Al-Soudah, bringing together centuries of heritage and a sense of place you will not find elsewhere. The ensemble is made up of three adjacent fortified palaces, each with its own name and symbolism—reflected across dozens of rooms and more than thirty-two chambers where meaning follows naming in authentic Aseeri tradition. A shared eastern balcony on the fourth floor links two of the palaces, opening onto green farmland and towering peaks.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP2: The fortresses were built from mountain stone with thick protective walls engineered to endure raids and harsh weather. Clever layouts made them sanctuaries in peacetime and strongholds in conflict, crowned by a single grand gate that unifies the complex with quiet majesty.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP3: For visitors, Al Abu Sirah is a standout cultural landmark: QR trails at chamber entrances deepen the storytelling, exhibitions and intimate displays bring crafts and arts to life, and seasonal performances fill the courtyards. Pause for coffee beside the palaces or share a memorable meal amid calm mountain air.

1.question: What does Aseer offer as a tourism destination?
1.answer: Aseer is one of Saudi Arabia’s standout regions, with varied landscapes—mountains, plains, wadis and coastlines—and different weather across seasons. It blends heritage architecture, festivals, modern urban hubs and cultural experiences across food, arts and fashion, with accommodation for many budgets and activities year-round.

2.question: When is the best time to visit Aseer?
2.answer: Spring and summer bring milder weather in the highlands plus lively events. Winter can be cool and misty in the mountains; autumn often offers calm hiking conditions.

3.question: What should I pack for Aseer?
3.answer: Pack layers for shifts between coast and mountains, comfortable shoes, sun protection and ID. Check any extra requirements for festivals or sites you plan to visit.

aboutAseer.title: About Aseer
aboutAseer.heroSubtitle: Discover the region's natural and cultural diversity.

story.sectionSubtitle: Across thousands of kilometres in southwestern Saudi Arabia, Aseer unfolds as a legendary story of astonishing chapters: mountain peaks crowned with clouds and draped in mist, green plains that promise bounty all year round, warm shores on the edge of a pristine sea, and a majestic desert in the silence and dignity of its grandeur—a natural tapestry steeped in ancient history, authentic culture, unique heritage, and generous hospitality. A destination where you can weave your own story of experience, adventure, exploration, and beauty.
story.sectionCaption: Discover Aseer to rediscover Saudi Arabia.

culture1.title: Land of culture and the arts
culture1.description: For lovers of authentic arts, Aseer is a rendezvous like no other. Its unique, varied character offers scenes found nowhere else. Its diverse landscape has shaped equally diverse artistic and performing traditions that harmonise with every mountain and coast, flowing sweetly across every valley and plateau. When an Aseeri man finds solitude, his flutes enchant the earth and sky; when the women of Aseer were shaped among their flowers, they created the colours of Al-Qatt and painted it on their walls until it became an art form listed as UNESCO intangible heritage; and when evening gatherings sweeten on mountain nights and breezes rise through the valleys, the Aseeri voice rises in song and blends with companions in dances rooted in the land like its wadis—arts that now fill festivals across the region. Aseer is also distinguished by the circular Qasab architecture reaching skyward: fortresses in times of war, grain stores safe from harm the rest of the year, still standing as witnesses to authentic arts waiting for you to experience them.

nature2.title: In Aseer, an exquisite symphony played by nature
nature2.description: As you move through Aseer from a mountain peak reaching 3,000 metres to shores at sea level, with plains, valleys, plateaus, and dunes between, you pass through different climates, mostly mild throughout the year, visited by rain in most seasons until it became a friend to every field and neighbour to every valley. Aseer paints a green natural canvas that includes more than half of the Kingdom's green areas, stretching 125 kilometres along the Red Sea coast, promising rich biodiversity with perennial trees, fruitful crops, and rare wildlife such as the Asir magpie in its mountains and gulls and flamingos on its shores. With this natural diversity and environmental wealth, Aseer draws a divine canvas of perfection and beauty, pulsing with everything wondrous—you need only discover that wonder yourself and return carrying the scent of nature within you.

heritage3.title: Aseer, a proud history
heritage3.description: If you are passionate about history, in Aseer you will find a story of more than seven centuries that refuses to fade or be forgotten—history embodied in towering war fortresses, castles steadfast against time and nature, and palaces that tell tales of glory once lived in and never left. In more than four thousand villages scattered like strings of pearls between its cities and governorates, history has taste and scent; between its lines you will read an ancient culture, exquisite arts, and the authenticity of a people of strong character and fierce courage, like their land in steadfastness and pride.

architectural4.title: Architectural heritage
architectural4.description: Aseer is one of the world's largest open-air museums, home to more than nine thousand heritage buildings across the Kingdom, including dozens of museums that warmly welcome thousands of visitors each year. Architecture in Aseer is a unique art in its final form, as varied as its terrain and climate, with design and building methods drawn from the land and human needs over hundreds of years—still standing today as majestic testimony to the capability of the Aseeri people and the genius of their architecture, which shaped a deep civilisation and history that does not fade.

culinaryArts5.title: Culinary arts
culinaryArts5.description: In Aseeri cuisine you will find everything to satisfy your senses from a single region: coffee from Aseeri coffee trees on the mountain slopes, Safri dates from the palms of Bisha, mountain wheat or plain sorghum with fresh milk and wildflower honey, and finally a dish of haneeth from herds raised between Aseer's plains and valleys. A culinary experience that brings mountains, plains, and coast to one table—from areekah and mashgothah to mifa bread from the tannur and marqoush.

aseerCommunity.subtitle: Stories and activities from the local community.

slider.sectionSubtitle: Aseer spans a wide geographic area with one of the highest population densities among Saudi regions, home to more than one million people.

slide1.title: Spirit of Aseer
slide1.description: Settlement across Aseer's mountain, coastal, Bedouin, and urban landscapes has not weakened deep-rooted customs, traditions, or the human qualities that define the region. Openness to progress and modernity blends with generosity, loyalty, and kindness alongside cultural and professional growth.

slide2.title: A connected community
slide2.description: The family is the heart of social life in Aseer—the first cradle of upbringing that nurtures authenticity and development. These bonds extend to relatives and friends united by warmth and loyalty, as coffee brings them together in moments of rest and evening gatherings.

slide3.title: A thriving life
slide3.description: Aseer society is rooted in a love of art expressed in dress, architecture, food, music, poetry, knowledge, and livelihoods from trade and farming. Geographic diversity enriched these arts while preserving heritage and pride in tradition.

dishesSection.title: Taste traditional Aseeri dishes
dishesSection.description: Aseeri cooking brings mountains, valleys, and farms together on one table: coffee from highland beans, dates from Bisha, mountain wheat and valley grains, fresh dairy, and wildflower honey—often finishing with slow-cooked haneeth from local herds. Explore dishes like haneeth, areekah, mashgothah, asidah, mifa bread from the tannur, marqoush bread, mabthoothah, and more.

background.section1Title: Aseer 2024 is the first World Region of Gastronomy Outside Europe
background.section1Body: In September 2022, Asir was declared the winner of the title of "World Culinary Arts Region 2024," making it the first region from outside Europe to win the title awarded by the International Institute of Culinary Arts, Culture, Arts and Tourism (IGCAT) to regions that joined the platform and met the criteria developed by the institute. These criteria include working across economic, cultural, social and environmental development sectors through the field of culinary arts to support sustainable regional development. The award was presented by the president of the institute, Diane Dodd, at an official ceremony held in Turin, Italy on September 24, 2022. This victory came after a jury of experts from the institute visited the region during the period (February 27 - March 1, 2022) and met with local stakeholders to assess Asir's readiness to hold the title. This visit reflected the region's efforts in supporting local cultural and food diversity, its endeavor to ensure regional biodiversity and protect the environment, preserve heritage and traditional knowledge, and empower young generations to create distinctive products and services to attract sustainable tourism.
background.mocCaption: Under the supervision of the Culinary Arts Commission
background.section2Body: The World Region of Gastronomy title from IGCAT recognises regions committed to preserving cultural heritage and developing tourism through food. It rewards cultural and environmental diversity, community support, and new generations through culinary innovation and integrated visitor services.

events.title: Featured events
events.discription: The Aseer region hosted the 27th meeting of the World Regions of Gastronomy Platform, where 20 international experts from 11 award-winning regions gathered to exchange best practices and explore local culture. This unique event, held for the first time outside Europe, featured discussions and workshops on the role of culinary arts in local development and sustainability promotion.

1.title: Tenth expert meeting in Aseer
1.description: Aseer hosted the 27th meeting of the World Regions of Gastronomy platform, bringing together 20 international experts from 11 awarded regions to exchange best practices and explore local culture through workshops on gastronomy and sustainable development.

card1.title: Honey Research Center - King Khalid University
card1.description: Visitors can discover the center's efforts to preserve local honey varieties that are an integral part of Aseer's environment. Research on beekeeping, honey production, and environmental sustainability is displayed, highlighting how new generations are engaged in this vital industry.

card2.title: Preservation Society of Bounty
card2.description: Visitors can learn about initiatives aimed at reducing food waste, as the society works to recycle excess food from restaurants and households, redistributing it to needy families. Success stories from the society, with over 16,000 volunteers, reflect the spirit of generosity and community cooperation in Aseer.

card3.title: South Women's Association
card3.description: The association has introduced innovative training programs to support local women in the fields of cooking and hospitality. These programs aim to economically empower women by providing them with the necessary skills to manage their own projects or join the workforce, thereby enhancing their independence and contributing to local development.

card4.title: Taste Street
card4.description: An immersive experience at Taste Street, where visitors can enjoy a variety of traditional dishes from local restaurants and households. The event provides an opportunity to explore the flavors of Aseer in a vibrant atmosphere that enhances social and cultural exchange.

card5.title: Wine Farm
card5.description: Exploring the first tourist farm in Aseer, where visitors can learn about the efforts to preserve local plants. The farm offers an interactive experience for guests, including guided tours and fresh dishes, making it an ideal destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

card1.title: Honey Cottage
card1.description: An inspiring experience at a family-owned honey farm specializing in beekeeping and honey production. The "Honey Cottage" stands out by blending traditions with innovation, housing 3,000 beehives scattered across Aseer. Visitors can sample the local honey while learning about its sustainable production methods that reflect the region's values.

card2.title: The Village of Rijal Almaa
card2.description: A visit to one of the most prominent heritage villages in the Kingdom, where the unique architecture of the village, made from stone and clay, was explored. Visitors learned about the region's cultural heritage through local museums and guided tours that provided a glimpse into daily life and the ancient Aseer traditions.

card1.title: Food Gift Challenge
card1.description: On the last day of the events, some members of the institute joined the judging panel for the "Global Food Gift Challenge" held at King Khalid University. The competition involved evaluating unique food products from various regions around the world, with winners selected based on criteria such as innovation, sustainability, and storytelling. The event gave special recognition to products that reflected the spirit of local heritage and culture.

card2.title: Workshop at the Aseer Development Authority
card2.description: On the final day, the remaining members of the institute visited the Aseer Development Authority, accompanied by representatives from the Saudi Tourism Authority and the Heritage Authority. The workshop included presentations on the master plan for the development of Aseer, including the Soudah Development Conservation Program to support the local juniper tree, as well as documenting the use of wild plants in cooking in collaboration with the Culinary Arts Commission. The aim of the workshop was to highlight strategies for preserving Aseer's environmental and cultural heritage.

card3.title: The Closing Ceremony
card3.description: The events of the 27th meeting of the World Culinary Arts Regions Platform concluded with an official ceremony at King Khalid University. The ceremony was an occasion to honor the efforts of local and international stakeholders during the events. It included the presentation of recognition awards and highlighted the key achievements of the Aseer region as part of its project to promote culinary arts and sustainable tourism.

5.title: Workshop to Activate the Role of Stakeholders
5.description: The Culinary Arts Commission organized the workshop "Aseer World Region of Gastronomy 2024" at King Khalid University in Al-Fara’a, where government entities, associations, and business owners gathered to work together on enhancing Aseer’s position as a global culinary destination. The workshop focused on showcasing achievements, highlighting the region’s potential to attract visitors through culinary arts, and developing innovative plans and sustainable initiatives for 2024 and 2025, making Aseer a key destination for flavor and culture enthusiasts.

1.name: Mayada Badr
1.quote: Aseer’s cuisine is a vibrant palette of flavors, textures, and aromas, deeply influenced by its geographical diversity and the agricultural dedication of its community. From the terraced fields to the verdant valleys, each landscape contributes uniquely to the region’s culinary repertoire. Dishes here are more than food; they are narratives of history, culture, and innovation passed down through generations. Ingredients such as indigenous herbs, grains, and fruits are transformed through time-honored methods into exquisite meals that echo the spirit of Aseer.

1.title: Adventures in Saudi Arabia: Taste of Aseer

2.title: Let's go to Aseer — MENA candidate regions for gastronomy

1.title: Al-Haneeth
1.description: Throughout the region, and especially along the coastal stretches like Mahayel and Rijal Alma, Haneeth is more than a meal; it is a symbol of hospitality and communal joy, a treasure shared during special gatherings. Recognized officially by the Culinary Arts Commission under the Ministry of Culture, Haneeth is not only a source of regional pride but also a cherished legacy, an emblem of cultural identity preserved for future generations.

2.title: Al-‘Areekah
2.description:
Al-Areekah, in its essence, captures the soul of Aseer's winters, serving as a warm embrace during the brisk mornings. Its appeal has woven through the fabric of local and regional cuisine, gracing the menus of numerous eateries, sometimes adorned with cream or nuts for a quick, yet soulful breakfast.
But it's in the governorates and the quaint villages of Aseer, like Khamis Mushait, Sarat Abidah, and Ahad Rufaida, that Al-Areekah truly shines as a beacon of hospitality. Here, it stands proud during the Al-Wasl period, a bridge between meals, embodying a tradition of warmth and welcome that is quintessentially Aseeri, making Al-Areekah not just a dish, but a cherished moment shared among friends and family.

3.title: Mifa Bread
3.description:
Crafted from the bountiful wheat fields of the Sarawat Mountains, Meyfa bread embodies the essence of tradition and sustenance, with some variations incorporating red corn grains, known as Al-Zaer, particularly prevalent in the Tihama regions where it is cultivated.
Esteemed as an indispensable staple in Aseer, Meyfa bread supplants commercial bread types, captivating the palates of all who partake in its wholesome goodness. Its allure is particularly pronounced during the holy month of Ramadan, where it reigns supreme on dining tables.

4.title: Al-Mashghoutha
4.description: Embraced as a quintessential winter delight, Al-Mashgootha captivates with its high caloric content, making it a favored choice among children, the elderly, patients, and during festive seasons, celebrated for its ease of consumption and nutritional richness. This esteemed dish serves as a symbol of generosity and hospitality, particularly cherished among the people of the Al-Hajar region in Aseer, including Al-Namas, Balasmar, Balahmar, and Tanuma
